hero.intro: Isolation, check and ball valves for refineries, gas plants, pipelines, power stations and process plant, built to API and ASME standards in carbon, alloy, stainless and duplex steel. Every valve is specified by size, pressure class, material and end connection, and supplied with its material certificates and pressure-test record.

guidance.heading: Start with the job the valve does
guidance.body: Gate and ball valves isolate: they run fully open or fully closed. Globe valves isolate and throttle, at the cost of a higher pressure drop. Check valves stop reverse flow on their own. Within each type, the pressure class follows the line rating, the body material follows the fluid and temperature, and the end connection follows the piping: raised-face or ring-joint flanges, or butt-weld ends matched to the pipe schedule.

standards.heading: Designed and tested to published standards
standards.body: Bodies are designed to ASME B16.34 for wall thickness and pressure-temperature rating. Gate valves follow API 600 (cast) and API 602 (forged); globe and swing check valves follow BS 1873 and BS 1868; dual-plate check valves API 594; pipeline ball, gate and check valves API 6D; floating ball valves ISO 17292. Flanges are to ASME B16.5, butt-weld ends to ASME B16.25 and face-to-face lengths to ASME B16.10.

items.q: Which pressure classes do you supply?
items.a: ASME Class 150 to 2500 across the range, with Class 4500 for pressure-seal gate, globe and check valves and forged valves. PN-rated valves are supplied where the piping is to EN 1092-1.

items.q: Can the valves be supplied with actuators?
items.a: Yes. Gear operators, and electric, pneumatic and hydraulic actuators, are fitted and tested on the valve before dispatch. Send the operating pressure, the supply available and the fail position.
Yes. Valves for sour service are built and certified to NACE MR0175 / ISO 15156 when the order calls for it. State the H2S partial pressure and the material requirement in the enquiry.

categories.name: Gate Valves

hero.intro: Gate valves for on-off isolation in process piping and pipelines. Cast steel wedge-gate valves to API 600 cover NPS 2" and up; forged valves to API 602 cover the small-bore lines; pressure-seal bonnets take the high-pressure, high-temperature duties; bellows seals stop stem emissions; slab and expanding gates serve pipelines to API 6D.

guidance.heading: Wedge, parallel slide or through-conduit
guidance.body: A flexible wedge suits most process isolation because it tolerates thermal and piping load. A parallel slide gate seals on line pressure and suits steam and high-temperature service. A through-conduit slab gate leaves a full, smooth bore for pigging and slurry. An expanding gate seals mechanically on both seats, so it holds in either flow direction.

items.q: Can a gate valve throttle flow?
items.a: No. Run partly open, the gate and seats erode and vibrate. Use a globe valve or a control valve to regulate flow, and keep gate valves fully open or fully closed.
Bolted bonnets are standard up to about Class 900. Above that, and in high-temperature steam, a pressure-seal bonnet uses line pressure to load the bonnet seal and keeps the valve compact.

categories.name: Globe Valves
categories.shortDescription: Cast steel globe valves to BS 1873 and forged globe valves to API 602: T, Y and angle pattern, bolted or pressure-seal bonnet, for throttling and tight shut-off.
categories.seoDescription: Cast steel globe valves to BS 1873 and forged API 602 globe valves, T, Y and angle pattern, NPS 1/2" to 36", Class 150 to 4500, bolted or pressure-seal bonnet.

hero.intro: Globe valves regulate flow as well as isolating it. The disc moves square to the seat, so it closes tight and throttles without the seat wear a gate would suffer. Cast steel valves to BS 1873 cover NPS 2" and up; forged valves to API 602 cover the small bores, in T, Y and angle patterns.

guidance.heading: T, Y or angle pattern
guidance.body: The T pattern is compact and the most common. The Y pattern straightens the flow path and cuts the pressure drop, which matters on steam and high-flow lines. The angle pattern replaces an elbow and a valve in one body. For frequent throttling, ask for a hardfaced or parabolic disc.

categories.name: Check Valves
categories.shortDescription: Swing, tilting-disc, dual-plate, axial-flow and forged lift check valves to BS 1868, API 594, API 6D and API 602, NPS 1/2" to 84".
categories.seoTitle: Industrial Check Valves — Swing, Dual-Plate, Axial Flow
categories.seoDescription: Swing check valves to BS 1868, dual-plate API 594, axial-flow API 6D, tilting-disc and forged lift check valves, NPS 1/2" to 84", Class 150 to 4500.

hero.intro: Check valves stop reverse flow without an operator. Swing checks suit most horizontal lines; dual-plate wafer checks save weight and space; axial-flow checks close fast and quietly on pump and compressor discharges; tilting-disc checks close quickly with a low cracking pressure; forged lift checks cover the small bores.

guidance.heading: Match the check to the flow
guidance.body: Where flow can reverse quickly, such as at a pump discharge or in parallel pump sets, choose a fast-closing design (axial-flow, dual-plate or tilting-disc) to limit slam and water hammer. Swing checks need enough steady flow to hold the disc fully open; pulsating flow wears the hinge. Tell us the flow rate and the pump arrangement and we will size it.

categories.name: Floating Ball Valves
categories.shortDescription: Floating ball valves to ISO 17292 and API 6D: cast end-entry and side-entry, forged two- and three-piece, metal-seated, jacketed, double block and bleed and three-way.
categories.seoTitle: Floating Ball Valves — ISO 17292, Soft & Metal Seated
categories.seoDescription: Floating ball valves to ISO 17292: cast and forged bodies, soft and metal seats, fire-safe to API 607, NPS 1/2" to 24", Class 150 to 2500.

hero.intro: In a floating ball valve the ball is held by the two seats and line pressure pushes it onto the downstream seat to seal. The design is simple and tight-shutting, which makes it the standard quarter-turn valve for smaller bores and lower classes. Soft seats give bubble-tight shut-off; metal seats take abrasive and high-temperature duty.

guidance.heading: Floating or trunnion mounted
guidance.body: As size and pressure rise, the force on a floating ball, and the torque to turn it, grows quickly. Floating ball valves are the economic choice up to about NPS 6" in the high classes and NPS 10" in Class 150 and 300. Beyond that, a trunnion-mounted ball valve carries the load on its stem bearings.

categories.name: Trunnion Mounted Ball Valves
categories.shortDescription: Trunnion mounted ball valves to API 6D: side-entry and top-entry, soft and metal seated, fully welded, double block and bleed, and pig launching and receiving valves.
categories.seoTitle: Trunnion Mounted Ball Valves — API 6D, NPS 2" to 60"
categories.seoDescription: API 6D trunnion mounted ball valves: side-entry, top-entry, fully welded, metal seated and DBB, NPS 2" to 60", Class 150 to 2500, fire-safe to API 607.

hero.intro: In a trunnion mounted ball valve the ball turns on fixed stem and trunnion bearings while spring-loaded seats seal against it. Torque stays low at large sizes and high pressure, and each seat seals on its own, which gives double block and bleed from one valve. The standard choice for pipelines, gas plants and large-bore process lines to API 6D.

guidance.heading: Side entry, top entry or fully welded
guidance.body: A side-entry split body is the most common and the most economical. A top-entry body can be opened in line for seat and seal maintenance without cutting it out. A fully welded body has no body joints that can leak and suits buried and pipeline service. Metal seats replace soft seats where the line carries solids or runs hot.

A check valve opens on forward flow and closes on its own when flow stops or reverses, protecting pumps, compressors and equipment downstream. No operator or power is needed; the closing speed and the flow needed to hold it open depend on the disc design.

products.title: Jacketed Ball Valve, Full Jacket
products.descriptionShort: Jacketed (steam or thermal-oil heated) ball valves: NPS 1/2" to 8", Class 150, one-piece full jacket keeps viscous and solidifying fluids such as sulphur, bitumen and polymer melt fluid in the valve.
products.descriptionLong:
For fluids that thicken or set when they cool: molten sulphur, bitumen, asphalt, heavy fuel oil, wax, resins and polymer melts. A heating jacket surrounds the body and is fed with steam or thermal oil, so the fluid in the valve stays at line temperature and the valve does not freeze shut.

In a floating ball valve the ball is held between two seats and line pressure pushes it onto the downstream seat to seal. A quarter turn opens or closes it, and the straight bore gives a low pressure drop when open.

Construction

  • Full heating jacket around the body, steam or thermal-oil connections
  • One-piece jacket, so no cold spots at body joints
  • Floating ball, soft or metal seats
  • Lever, gear operator or actuator

Sizes and ratings
